fields.description: The walk-in's own phone number, captured at payment time. All Cash Customer walk-ins share the one Customer record (see SHARED_CASH_CUSTOMER_NAME), so this is what keeps their unallocated advance/credit from pooling across unrelated people. Blank for Invoice Customers, who already have their own distinct Customer record.
fields.label: Customer Phone

fields.description: Set when this payment was taken as a deposit against a Quotation before a Job Card existed for it — lets an unallocated deposit be traced back to, and later applied against, the Job Card eventually created for this Quotation.
fields.label: Quotation

fields.description: Split this payment across one or more job cards. Any amount left unallocated is treated as the customer's advance / credit.
fields.label: Job Card Allocations

fields.description: The submitted Payment Entry this receipt/refund actually posted to Cash/Bank and Debtors.
fields.label: Payment Entry

fields.description: Set on the ORIGINAL row once it has been superseded by a correction. Its Payment Entry is cancelled and it is excluded from every balance, credit and total computation, but the row itself is never edited — it stays as the immutable record of what was first captured. See correct_payment in api.py.
fields.label: Is Corrected

fields.description: The replacement Payments row that supersedes this one. NOTE: Payments.autoname is "autoincrement", so a Payments name is an int while this Link column is varchar — str() both sides on every write and filter (same trap as _get_job_card_allocated_payments).
fields.label: Corrected By Payment

fields.description: When the correction was made. Explicit rather than relying on `modified`, because the flagging write uses update_modified=False so this row's `modified` keeps reading as the moment the payment was originally captured.
fields.label: Corrected On

fields.description: Who made the correction. Explicit for the same reason as Corrected On — `modified_by` is deliberately left untouched.
fields.label: Corrected By

fields.description: Set on the REPLACEMENT row: the original payment this one corrects. Its presence is what marks a row as a correction. Same int-vs-varchar trap as Corrected By Payment — str() both sides.
fields.label: Corrects Payment

fields.description: Why the original was wrong. Mandatory at correction time — it is the only record of the reason, since neither Payments row carries the before/after diff on its own.
fields.label: Correction Reason
